item.title: Anthropic researcher resigns amid AI safety concerns
item.description: A researcher at the AI company Anthropic resigned with a warning that the entire artificial intelligence industry is designing tools that humans will soon lose control of.
item.content:encoded: A researcher at the AI company Anthropic resigned with a warning that the entire artificial intelligence industry is designing tools that humans will soon lose control of.

item.title: Fold the phone: Apple's new CEO unveils a foldable iPhone
item.description: New Apple CEO John Ternus announces the iPhone Duo, which folds like a passport and is the most radical iPhone design update in nearly 20 years.
item.content:encoded:
New Apple CEO John Ternus announces the iPhone Duo, which folds like a passport and is the most radical iPhone design update in nearly 20 years.

item.title: Australian social media users to be offered choice to opt out of algorithms
item.description: A government statement said on Tuesday social media platforms would be required to send a notification to new and existing users offering them a choice over their default feed.
item.content:encoded:
A government statement said on Tuesday social media platforms would be required to send a notification to new and existing users offering them a choice over their default feed.

(Image credit: Rick Rycroft)

item.title: Voters are fed up with data centers. Both parties are trying to cash in for midterms
item.description: Democrats and Republicans have found common ground in this campaign season. Both parties have poured millions into ads attacking data centers as the public continues to protest the AI facilities.

item.title: New Jersey asks Supreme Court to resolve fight over Kalshi's future
item.description: If the high court accepts the petition, it would tee up a case with sweeping implications for prediction markets, an industry that has unleashed billions of dollars of betting across nearly every aspect of modern life.

item.title: Understanding the tech giants' oversized influence in American schools
item.description: Big tech companies like Apple and Microsoft use devices, training and conferences for teachers and students to embed in schools. The New York Times' Natasha Singer discusses the impact in Coding Kids.

item.title: New lawsuits claim OpenAI execs put image ahead of safety in Canadian mass shooting
item.description: The suits say that recommendations to alert police about the alleged shooter were nixed by OpenAI's global affairs team, led by veteran political strategist Chris Lehane. OpenAI denies the claims.

item.title: Kalshi bans former congressman George Santos for life after State of the Union trades
item.description: Kalshi says Santos did not cooperate with its investigation into bets he placed on his own attendance at the State of the Union. The company also fined the disgraced congressman more than $71,000.

item.title: Are you sure that Kimmel clip was real? Late-night AI deepfakes are spreading online
item.description: While social media is rife with AI celebrity deepfakes, videos featuring late night TV hosts like Jimmy Kimmel and Jon Stewart are are easier to create than other kinds of deepfakes and potentially more disruptive.
